captions.instagram:
How does a ring light work?

Why does a circle of tiny LEDs make a face look so smooth? Trace the shadows a ring fills in, find its reflection in an eye, mix warm and cool light, and watch a cheap dimmer paint dark bands across a phone video.

→ A ring light is a circle of tiny LEDs behind a milky cover, with the camera in the middle.
→ One small lamp to the side throws a hard, dark nose shadow.
→ Wrap the light round the lens and every shadow is filled from the other side.
→ The wet front of the eye is a tiny curved mirror, so the ring shows up as a circle in it.
→ Twice as far from the light means about a quarter of the brightness.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/ringlightclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a ring light work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Why does a circle of tiny LEDs make a face look so smooth? Trace the shadows a ring fills in, find its reflection in an eye, mix warm and cool light, and watch a cheap dimmer paint dark bands across a phone video.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/ringlightclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/ringlightclear

In this video:
• A circle of LEDs. A ring light is a flat ring-shaped board of a hundred or more tiny white LEDs, half warm and half cool, behind a milky diffuser, with the camera looking through the hole.
• Why a ring fills shadows. A small lamp to one side leaves a hard nose shadow.
• The circle in the eye, and lux. The cornea is a convex mirror with a focal length near 3.9 mm, so a 26 cm ring at 50 cm shows up as a circle about 2 mm wide.
• Warm, cool and true. Each white LED is a blue chip under yellow phosphor.
• Dimming and dark bands. Cheap dimmers blink the LEDs fully on and off (PWM).
• Use it well. Raise the ring a little and the glare slides off spectacle lenses.
